I closed the tab, turned off my phone, and I'm just lying in the dark under my blanket hoping time stops so I never have to look at that screen. The absolute dread of seeing a low number and having to explain it to my older brother who was a branch topper is literally making me throw up.

I completely botched the frontend demo for our software engineering group project today and let down my entire team. They were all so nice about it, saying 'it's fine, we can fix it in the next sprint', which honestly makes it ten times worse because I know they're secretly blaming me for losing marks. I left the laboratory WhatsApp group, turned off my phone, and I'm planning to skip the next three classes because the thought of sitting next to them in the lecture hall makes me feel physically sick with shame.

I literally locked myself in the hostel toilet during the Day 1 placement PPT. Everyone in my wing is talking about their 12 LPA base offers and I couldn't even clear the coding round for a basic service company. I lied to my roommate saying I had food poisoning just so I didn't have to face the interviewers and get rejected in front of everyone.

The results portal went live yesterday and I haven't clicked the link. My dad keeps WhatsApping me asking for my SGPA because my cousin got a 9.4 at his college. I’m just pretending my internet is down in the hostel, but my hands are literally shaking because I know I probably cleared only three subjects and failed the rest.

During the DSA lab today, the external asked me a basic question about red-black trees and my mind just went totally blank. Everyone in my batch was staring, and I just stood up, said I was feeling sick, and walked out. I'm sitting in the library staircase right now, crying, because I know I'll get a zero for this viva, but staying there and looking that dumb was just impossible.

I lied to my group project partners and told them I cleared my backend backlog last sem, but I actually got an F again. Now they are planning to use that framework for our final year project and I'm freaking out because I don't know anything. I want to just drop out or ghost the entire group because telling them the truth is going to make them look at me like I'm some kind of charity case.

The Google and Microsoft referral forms are open but I didn't even click them. My friends are polishing their resumes and discussing Leetcode hard questions, but I just slept through the weekend. It's better to not apply and pretend I didn't care than to apply, get rejected in the first online assessment, and have my parents ask why my friends got in and I didn't.

I skipped the mock interview slot today and lied to my placement coordinator saying I had a high fever. Honestly, I was just staring at the DSA problems in the prep sheet, realizing I couldn't even code a simple BFS/DFS without looking at the solution, and the thought of some interviewer looking at my resume and asking why I have a 7.2 CGPA made my stomach turn. I've locked myself in my hostel room and ignored my mom's calls because she's going to ask if I cleared the round.

I didn't show up for the lab viva today. I stood outside the systems lab for fifteen minutes, watching my batchmates discuss their answers, and I just couldn't walk in. If the external examiner realized I couldn't write the shell script, I think I would have died right there. Now I'll probably get an F-grade and have a backlog on my transcript forever, but in that moment, disappearing felt so much easier than facing the humiliation.

My dad sent a screenshot of our neighbor's son getting a 45 LPA package at a fintech firm to our family WhatsApp group, with just a thumbs-up emoji. I literally closed my IDE, went to bed, and slept for 14 hours straight. I have my own McKinsey shortlist announcement tomorrow and I'm already planning to turn off my phone and sleep through it, because if my name isn't on that PDF, I won't be able to look my parents in the eye.

Everyone in my wing is talking about their summer internship conversions, and I'm just sitting here pretending to be sick so I don't have to join them for dinner in the mess. I got rejected in the final HR round yesterday because I fumbled my words, and the thought of them asking me 'bro, what happened?' makes me want to throw up. I'd rather they think I'm antisocial than know I was the only one who didn't make the cut.

I got a backlog in my 3rd semester math paper and I haven't told a single soul, not even my roommate. Registering for the remedial exam is next week, but every time I open the portal, my hands shake and I close the tab because seeing 'F' next to my roll number makes me feel completely worthless. I'm thinking of skipping the registration deadline entirely and dealing with the consequences next year, just so I don't have to face the reality of it right now.

I skipped the day-1 placement presentation today. I literally hid in the library washroom for two hours because I knew my name wasn't on the shortlist for the high-frequency trading firm, and I couldn't bear to look my hostel mates in the eye. They all think I'm some coding god because I spent 10 hours a day on LeetCode, but the truth is I got filtered out in the first round of resume screening itself. I can't even face my parents' WhatsApp group messages asking how the first day went, so I'm thinking of just pretending I'm sick and staying in my room for the rest of the week.

I didn't turn up for the Operating Systems lab viva today. I practiced the shell scripts all night, but when I saw my batchmates confidently discussing their output screens outside the lab, my chest went completely tight and I felt like throwing up. I knew the moment the external examiner looked at my code and called it junk, I'd just break down in front of forty people. I walked right out of the building and spent the last three hours riding the local train back and forth, and now I'll probably get a backlog just because I couldn't face a five-minute evaluation.

My cousin just bagged a 24 LPA package at an MNC, and my dad immediately posted it on our family group with the caption 'so proud of our family's brightest star.' I scraped by with a 6.8 CGPA this semester, and I've been actively ignoring my dad's calls for the last three days because I know he'll ask about my semester results. I feel like an absolute fraud eating dinner at the hostel mess when my parents are spending their hard-earned money on a failure who can't even clear the cutoffs for basic mass recruiters. I just want to disappear into the ground so they never have to feel embarrassed of me again.

Everyone in my wing is talking about their Google Step internships and how they cracked their Leetcode hards, and I'm sitting here struggling to even balance a binary search tree. I started lying to them, telling them I'm preparing for some niche research fellowships just so they'd stop asking me about my coding ranks. I know the lies are going to catch up to me when the placement season ends and I'm the only one without an offer, but the shame of being the dumbest guy in the wing is literally eating me alive. I’ve started locking my door and staying in the dark so I don't have to join their hallway chats.

I saw the grade sheet for the math midterm posted on the notice board today and my roll number was right at the bottom with a single digit score. I saw my friends crowd around the board, laughing at the 'low scores' without realizing one of those was mine, and I just turned around and ran back to my room before they could see me. I can't face tomorrow's tutorial class because the professor hands back the physical papers in person and calls out the marks. I’m thinking of emailing him some fake medical certificate just so I don't have to stand up in front of everyone and receive my failing paper.
